label: Almost Complex Structures
notes: Chapter four runs across printed pages 152 to 190 and turns the symplectic form into a partner for complex geometry. An almost complex structure J multiplies tangent vectors by i, and when it agrees with omega it manufactures a Riemannian metric, the bridge we exploit all chapter.

label: What Is an Almost Complex Structure
notes: A bundle endomorphism J of the tangent bundle squaring to minus the identity is the defining datum. On each fibre it acts like multiplication by i, so every tangent space becomes a complex vector space and the manifold must be even dimensional to admit one.

label: J Rotates the Tangent Plane
notes: Geometrically J is a quarter turn of every tangent plane: applying it twice reverses a vector, which is exactly the equation J squared equals minus the identity. The picture of a vector rotated ninety degrees and then to its antipode is the whole intuition behind the algebra.

label: Taming and Compatibility
notes: A form tames J when omega of v with Jv is strictly positive on nonzero vectors, fixing an orientation of the planes. Compatibility adds symmetry, omega of Jv and Jw equals omega of v and w, so the two conditions sit nested with compatibility the stronger demand.

label: The Induced Metric
notes: Compatibility lets us define g of v and w as omega of v with Jw. Symmetry and positivity make g a genuine Riemannian metric, so a single triple omega, J, g locks together the symplectic, complex, and metric worlds. This is the central construction of the chapter.

label: The Space of Compatible Structures
notes: Write J of M and omega for all compatible almost complex structures. For a fixed symplectic form this space is always nonempty and, crucially, contractible. Contractibility means any J can be deformed to any other, so invariants built from J never depend on the arbitrary choice.

label: Integrability and the Nijenhuis Tensor
notes: An almost complex structure is integrable when it comes from honest holomorphic charts. The obstruction is the Nijenhuis tensor N, an antisymmetric expression built from Lie brackets of J. When N vanishes identically the rotation field is rigid enough to assemble local complex coordinates.

label: Newlander-Nirenberg
notes: The Newlander-Nirenberg theorem closes the loop: J is integrable, the Nijenhuis tensor vanishes, and the manifold is a genuine complex manifold are all equivalent statements. A hard analytic theorem turns a pointwise tensor identity into the global existence of holomorphic coordinate charts.

label: Kahler Manifolds
notes: A Kahler manifold is the integrable compatible case: omega closed, J integrable, and the two compatible through g. Equivalently the complex structure is parallel for the Levi-Civita connection. Kahler geometry is the rich overlap where symplectic, complex, and Riemannian structures all coexist harmoniously.

label: The Kahler Lattice
notes: Picture three overlapping conditions. Symplectic plus complex compatible gives Kahler at their intersection. The inclusions of tame inside taming and compatible inside tame organize the structures into a lattice, with Kahler sitting at the most constrained and most fertile bottom corner.

label: Dimension Two Is Special
notes: On a symplectic surface every compatible almost complex structure is automatically integrable, so every almost complex surface is Kahler. The Nijenhuis obstruction has no room to be nonzero in two real dimensions, collapsing the distinctions that genuinely matter in higher dimensions.

label: J-Holomorphic Curves
notes: A J-holomorphic curve is a map u from a Riemann surface whose differential commutes with the structures, du composed with j equals J composed with du. This nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann equation launches the moduli theory that powers Gromov-Witten invariants and modern symplectic topology.
